text:
maria_sales: Heads-up: MediCorp signed the NDA and wants a 48-72h POC next week. Theyhave an on-prem cluster that must reach our Private endpoint. They're asking whether PrivateLink (interface endpoint) or VPC peering to our transit account is faster to set up and what we can provide for an initial smoke key.

devin_se: PrivateLink is usually faster for customers who don't want to touch route tables on our side. For on-prem -> cloud path they'll either terminate via a customer VPC that has a VPCE, or go through a TGW if they already use that. Important: if they go through an S2S VPN to a VPC, the VPCE still works (traffic is inside AWS), but DNS needs attention.

ash_infra: Quick infra constraints:
- VPCE (interface) requires subnets in each AZ you want HA in (recommend 2 AZs)
- Security group on the VPCE must allow inbound 443 from whatever source (their VPC CIDR or on-prem CIDR if routed)
- For VPC peering: MUST be non-overlapping CIDRs. Peering requires RT changes on both sides.
- If they're using TGW, we can accept routes to our service CIDR through TGW attachments.

rachel_sec: Security: we cannot provide a long-lived account API key for a POC. Options: time-limited API token bound to their org id (recommended) or a short-lived API key we rotate daily. Also ask them to provide their egress firewall rules so we can confirm whether 443 TLS to our endpoint or outbound to our control plane is allowed.

maria_sales: They also asked about DNS: "If we create a VPCE and enable private DNS will the SDK automatically resolve private-api.redwood-inference.internal to the endpoint?"

devin_se: Yes, with Private DNS enabled the regional CNAMEs resolve to the interface ENIs. However, if their on-prem DNS is authoritative and not forwarding to AWS resolver, they'll need to create a split-horizon entry or forward the redwood domain to the VPC resolver (route 169.254.169.253 in some setups) or use host-level /etc/hosts during the POC.

ash_infra: Example VPCE create command we hand to customers (they run in their AWS account):
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abcd1234 \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-abc123xyz \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --subnet-ids subnet-0a subnet-0b \
  --security-group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d \
  --private-dns-enabled
```
Then test with: `dig +short private-api.redwood-inference.internal` (should return ENI IPs). If dig returns public IPs, they didn't enable private DNS or their resolver is bypassing AWS.

ben_ops: For the smoke API key test, we can issue an ephemeral token valid for 12 hours and restrict it to the POC org + rate limit. We'll log issuance and alert on abnormal use. We'll need a signed customer contact and the account id to map tokens.

rachel_sec: Also capture whether they require TLS client certs or mTLS. We currently support mTLS for Private endpoints if requested, but that's an enterprise opt-in and will add ~2 business days to setup.

maria_sales: Good note. They want a simple curl test example once VPCE is up.

devin_se: Example curl (using ephemeral token):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL_TOKEN>" \
  https://private-api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/healthz
```
Expect 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"}. If TLS SNI fails, ensure their clients send the proper host header and that private DNS resolves to ENI IPs.

ash_infra: Peering path notes (if customer insists):
- Create peering connection (customer creates, we accept)
- Update their route table: destination 10.200.0.0/16 -> pcx-xxxxx
- Update our transit RT back to their CIDR (if required)
- Ensure NACLs allow return traffic (65k ephemeral ports)
- No automatic DNS integration; they'd need to add records or use inbound resolver.

ben_ops: Action on tokens: I'll prepare a single-use ephemeral token flow today and a short README on how our token service works (rotate, revoke).

rachel_sec: I'll prepare a minimal audit artifact: list of IPs used by our service, expected ports (443 TLS), token policy, and a one-page threat model. Share with their security team.

maria_sales: Copying the action items: 
- ben_ops: ephemeral token flow + README (EOD)
- ash_infra/devin_se: VPCE CLI + DNS troubleshooting steps + test commands (ASAP)
- rachel_sec: security artifact & mTLS note (today)
- maria_sales: schedule kickoff and confirm their on-prem DNS approach (tomorrow AM)

deploy_bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privatelink-onprem-poc (contains checklist, SG templates, example RTs).

maria_sales: Thanks team. I'll send the contact info to get their AWS account id and their on-prem DNS owner. Ping here when you drop the snippets. :white_check_mark:
